The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 427, 447, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sec.33(A) of BDA Act.

2. Prosecution Case: The accused No.1 to 4 have illegally trespassed into the Survey No.1/2 situated at Geddalahalli, within the limits of Sanjayanagar Police Station, destroyed the name board and fence wire and constructed compound wall with an intention to cheat BDA authority and grab BDA property by violating the order of Hon'ble High Court to maintain the status quo in the said property which belongs to Bangalore Development Authority and caused damaged to BDA property.
3. First Information Report:

Upon the receipt of first information from CW1, CW10/PW2 Sri Narasimhaiah, PSI of Sanjay Nagara Police Station registered Crime No.04/2013 against accused persons for the offences punishable under Section 427, 420, 447 R/W Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.33(A)
of BDA Act, prepared FIR as per Ex.P3, drawn spot mahazar on 03-01-2013 as per Ex.P4 from 9.00 a.m. KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 to 9.30 am in the presence of CW2 namely Sri Mahesh Kumar and CW3 namely Sri Narendra Kumar.
4.
Investigation:

Thereafter, PW2 recorded the statements of requisite witnesses, secured the documents from BDA through letter as per Ex.P5 and collected the photographs of alleged spot from CW1 and on completion of investigation, he filed charge sheet against accused for the alleged offences.

5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court had taken cognizance for the offences alleged against the accused No.1 to 4.
6.
The accused No.1 to 4 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 04-01-2017.

7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused No.1 to 4.
8.

Charge: After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused No.1 to 4, charge for the offence punishable U/Sec.447, 427, 420 read with Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 33(A) of B.D.A.

sentences.text: 9. In view of the continuous absence of accused No.3, the case against her was split up by the order dated 29-12-2025.
10. Prosecution Evidence: The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 10 witnesses, examined 3 witnesses and exhibited 5 documents and closed their side.

The presence of CW3 and CW4 and CW5 and CW6 could not be secured and was dropped out by the order dated 19/08/2024,
29/08/2025 and 13/01/2026 after due execution of proclamation.

The process of proclamation against CW7 to CW9 returned unexecuted and hence given up from the examination of CW7 to CW9 by the order dated 13/01/2026.
11. Statement of Accused as per section 313 of CrPC: After completion of evidence of prosecution,
the accused No.1, 2 and 4 were examined as per section 313 of Cr.P.C wherein they denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witnesses and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

13. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1, 2 and 4 along with split up accused No.3 have illegally trespassed into the Survey No.1/2 of Geddalahalli within the limits of Sanjayanagar Police Station which belongs to Bangalore Development Authority thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Section 447 read with Sec.34 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1, 2 and 4 along with split up accused No.3 have illegally trespassed into the above KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 said property and destroyed the name board and iron fence therein and constructed compound wall to the said property and caused damage to BDA property thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Section 427 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
3.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1, 2 and 4 along with split up accused No.3 have illegally trespassed into the site and constructed a compound wall with the intention to cheat BDA authority and grab BDA property by violating the order of the Hon'ble High Court to maintain the status quo in Survey No.1/1 of Geddalahalli which belongs to Bangalore Development Authority thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Section KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 420 read with Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.33(A) of BDA Act?
4. What order?

The Court's findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 to 3 : In the negative Point No.4 : As per final order REASONS 15. Point No.1 to 3:
These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 13 of this judgment, the prosecution examined the witnesses which are as follows i. CW9 Sri Giriyappa,
Gangman in BBMP examined as PW1 deposed that about 13 years ago, the fence wire and name plate placed in an empty place in Geddalahalli which were removed by him and CW10 as per the instruction of CW1 and CW7.

In this regard, the learned Senior APP has cross examined this witness by treating him as hostile witness KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 however no favorable answer has been elicited from him to support the prosecution case.

His denial of statement given before the police is marked as per Ex.P1.
ii.

CW11 Sri S.Narasimhaiah, the then PSI of Sanjay Nagara PS, examined as PW2 deposed that,
after receipt of complaint as per Ex.P2 from CW1, he registered FIR as per Ex.P3, drawn spot mahazar on 03-01-2013 as per Ex.P4 from 9.00 a.m. to 9.30 am in the presence of CW2 namely Sri Mahesh Kumar and CW3 namely Sri Narendra Kumar, recorded the statements of requisite witnesses, secured the documents from BDA through letter as per Ex.P5 and collected the photographs of alleged spot from CW1 and after investigation, he filed charge sheet against accused for the alleged offences.
iii. CW1

Sri G.K.Vishwanath, being informant examined as PW3 deposed that, on 01-01-2013, whilst going towards Geddalahalli village for inspection of the work, he came across an unauthorized compound wall being constructed in Survey No.1/1 as the Hon'ble High Court had ordered that the status quo be maintained in the said property, he stopped the work and lodged the complaint with the Sanjayanagar Police Station as per Ex.P2.
He identified his signature on spot mahazar as per Ex.P4 and he does not know who KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 were all present at the time of drawing mahazar as per Ex.P4.
Except the above facts he does not know other fact of the case.

In this regard, the learned Senior APP has cross examined this witness by treating him as hostile witness and admitted that Survey No.1/1 was acquired by the Authority for the purpose of constructing the Raj Mahal Vilas Layout, since there were no cases in Survey No. 1/2, they had taken possession of the same by putting up barbed wire around the same and installed the Authority's nameplate, and that a small barbed wire fence and the Authority's nameplate had been removed as per the order of the Hon'ble High Court.
Despite the order to maintain the status quo, compound wall was being constructed in Survey No. 1/1.
It is admitted that photographs were taken in this regard and that compound wall was being constructed in Survey No. 1/1, which was acquired.
16. The charges framed against accused No.1 to 4 is under Sec. 420 of IPC.

To hold a person guilty of cheating, it must be shown that the accused persons had a fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making representation or promise and there must be a culpable intention at the time of making a promise.
The culpable intention cannot be presumed, merely because, they failed to keep up the promise subsequently.

The ingredients required for constituting an offence of cheating have been clearly laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Ram Jas v. State of U.P. reported in [1970(2) SCC 740], which read as follows:
"(i) there should be fraudulent or dishonest inducement of a person by deceiving him;
(ii) (a) the person so deceived should be induced to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property; or (b) the person so deceived should be intentionally induced to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived; and (iii) in cases covered by (ii)(b), the act or omission should be one which causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to the person induced in body, mind, reputation or property."

Thus, it is clear that the subject land survey No.1/1 measuring 0.28 guntas belongs to the father of accused No.1 Sri Narayana Raj and has filed the case before the Hon'ble High court of Karnakata.

Such being the case, violation of interim order of status quo in W. P. No.14731-16738/2010 does not amount to cheating rather would amounts to contempt of court as no deception or inducement from the accused No.1 to 4 to the PW3.
19.

Added to which, the basic ingredients of cheating i.e., inducement and fraudulent or dishonest intention were not made out from the complaint averments or from the contents of charge sheet KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 except the accused violated the interim order by putting fencing wire in survey No. 1/1 during the existence of status quo order thereby the prosecution failed to prove the ingredients of offence under section 420 of IPC.

21.
The next accusation is under section 447 of IPC which reads as under Sec. 447 of IPC.

Punishment for criminal trespass.-- Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

So far as the offence under Sec 447 of Indian Penal Code is concerned, to satisfy the offence under Section 447, the prosecution should prove that there is a criminal trespass, as defined under Section 441 of the Indian Penal Code.

To bring home an offence under Section 441 of the Indian Penal Code, the prosecution should establish,
entering into or upon property in possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property and the aim or dominant intention of the accused must be proved for committing an offence or intimidation, insult or annoyance.
22. To bring home an offence under Section 447 of the Indian Penal Code, no material produced by the prosecution/PW3 that the accused No.1 to 4 has criminally trespassed into the BDA's property or entered upon the property of BDA with an intention to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy 23.

To establish that the accused No.1 to 4 have trespassed into survey No.1/1 and put up the compound wall in the survey No.1/1 belongs to BDA KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 property within extent of 0.28 guntas, no materials furnished by the prosecution except producing photographs and sketch however the said sketch lacks the substance of putting up the compound wall by the accused No. 1 to 4 whether the said fencing wire was within the 0.28 guntas of land alleged to have belongs to BDA.

Though the PW3 has lodged the complaint that BDA property has been trespassed however IO/PW2 and PW3 did not not collect any supporting document during investigation to corroborate that the said fencing wire was within the 0.28 guntas of land alleged to have belongs to BDA in survey No. 1/1 thereby the prosecution failed to prove the ingredients of offence under section 447 of IPC.
therefore the point No. 1 is answered in negative.
25. The next charge is under section 427 of IPC which reads as under Sec. 427 of IPC. Mischief causing damage to the amount of fifty rupees.--

Whoever commits mischief and thereby causes loss or damage to the amount of fifty rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Now coming to whether the ingredients of Section 427 of IPC are fulfilled.

425 of IPC defines mischief and the essential ingredients are as follows:
1 (1)Whoever (2)with intent to cause or knowing that he is likely to cause (3)Wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person (4)causes destruction of any property or any such change in the property which destroys or diminishes its value or utility or affects it injuriously, is said to commit mischief.

Unless the estimation for loss to the BDA is established in survey No.1/1, this court cannot come to a conclusion that the accused No.1 to 4 has caused loss or damage to the property of BDA thereby the prosecution failed to prove the ingredients of offence under section 427 of IPC.
Therefore the point No.2 is answered in negative.

26. Even considering the nature of allegations in the complaint, this court is of the opinion that no case is made out for taking cognizance of offences under Section 420, 447, 427 of Indian Penal Code and Section 33A of Bangalore Development Authority.

The case involves a property dispute between the BDA and the father of accused No.1 Sri Narayana KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 Raju,
the criminal law set into motion by the CW1/PW3.
27.

It appears from the record that when there is a violation of interim order of status quo, the contempt proceedings could have been initiated against the accused No.1 to 4 however no such steps were taken.

At this juncture, it is profitable to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of G.Sagar Suri v. State of U.P reported in 2000(2) SCC 636 wherein it has been held that the criminal proceedings is not a short cut remedy, when other remedies are available in law and in the case of the Commissioner of Police and Ors. vs. Devender Anand and Ors reported in AIR 2019 SUPREME COURT 3807 held that the criminal proceedings initiated by Original complainant is nothing but an abuse of the process of law for settling a civil dispute thereby the accused is entitled for an order of acquittal.

of BDA Act, prepared FIR as per Ex.P3, drawn spot mahazar on 03-01-2013 as per Ex.P4 from 9.00 a.m. KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 to 9.30 am in the presence of CW2 namely Sri Mahesh Kumar and CW3 namely Sri Narendra Kumar.

9. In view of the continuous absence of accused No.3, the case against her was split up by the order dated 29-12-2025.
The presence of CW3 and CW4 and CW5 and CW6 could not be secured and was dropped out by the order dated 19/08/2024,
29/08/2025 and 13/01/2026 after due execution of proclamation.

opennyai_summary.issue:
13. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.
Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1, 2 and 4 along with split up accused No.3 have illegally trespassed into the Survey No.1/2 of Geddalahalli within the limits of Sanjayanagar Police Station which belongs to Bangalore Development Authority thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Section 447 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1, 2 and 4 along with split up accused No.3 have illegally trespassed into the above KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 said property and destroyed the name board and iron fence therein and constructed compound wall to the said property and caused damage to BDA property thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Section 427 read with Sec.34 of IPC?
3.
Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1, 2 and 4 along with split up accused No.3 have illegally trespassed into the site and constructed a compound wall with the intention to cheat BDA authority and grab BDA property by violating the order of the Hon'ble High Court to maintain the status quo in Survey No.1/1 of Geddalahalli which belongs to Bangalore Development Authority thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Section KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 420 read with Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.33(A) of BDA Act?
4. What order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
16. The charges framed against accused No.1 to 4 is under Sec. 420 of IPC.
To hold a person guilty of cheating, it must be shown that the accused persons had a fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making representation or promise and there must be a culpable intention at the time of making a promise.
The culpable intention cannot be presumed, merely because, they failed to keep up the promise subsequently.
The specific case of prosecution is that the accused No.1 to 4 has encroached the property of BDA which is situated the Survey No.1/2 situated at Geddalahalli, within the limits of Sanjayanagar Police Station, destroyed the name board and fence wire and constructed compound wall with an intention to cheat BDA authority and grab BDA property by violating the order of Hon'ble High Court to maintain the status quo in the said property when the order of status quo was maintained by the order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bangalore in W.P.No. 14731-16738/2010 with intention to grab the property belongs to BDA thereby, committed the offence of cheating punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code however it is the specific defence of the accused No. 1 to 4 that the land survey No.1/1 of Geddalahalli, Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore belongs to the accused No.1's father Sri Narayana Raj and the said fact was admitted by the representative of BDA Sri G.K.Vishwanath (CW1/PW3) that Cross examination of PW3 by the accused

Such being the case, violation of interim order of status quo in W. P. No.14731-16738/2010 does not amount to cheating rather would amounts to contempt of court as no deception or inducement from the accused No.1 to 4 to the PW3.
19.
Added to which, the basic ingredients of cheating i.e., inducement and fraudulent or dishonest intention were not made out from the complaint averments or from the contents of charge sheet KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 except the accused violated the interim order by putting fencing wire in survey No. 1/1 during the existence of status quo order thereby the prosecution failed to prove the ingredients of offence under section 420 of IPC.
20. Section 33A of Bangalore Development Authority Act which reads as under [33A. Prohibition of unauthorized occupation of land.-
Sanction of prosecution.-No prosecution for any offence punishable under this Act shall be instituted except with the previous sanction of the Authority.
When no sanction is obtained from the Government of Karnataka to prosecute under Section 33A of BDA Act, there cannot be prosecution against the accused No. 1 to 4 in respect of Section 33A of BDA Act and the said principle is appreciated in the case of Smt. Susheela Narayan Vs State of Karnataka in Crl.
To bring home an offence under Section 441 of the Indian Penal Code, the prosecution should establish,
entering into or upon property in possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property and the aim or dominant intention of the accused must be proved for committing an offence or intimidation, insult or annoyance.
22. To bring home an offence under Section 447 of the Indian Penal Code, no material produced by the prosecution/PW3 that the accused No.1 to 4 has criminally trespassed into the BDA's property or entered upon the property of BDA with an intention to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy 23.
To establish that the accused No.1 to 4 have trespassed into survey No.1/1 and put up the compound wall in the survey No.1/1 belongs to BDA KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 property within extent of 0.28 guntas, no materials furnished by the prosecution except producing photographs and sketch however the said sketch lacks the substance of putting up the compound wall by the accused No. 1 to 4 whether the said fencing wire was within the 0.28 guntas of land alleged to have belongs to BDA.
Unless the estimation for loss to the BDA is established in survey No.1/1, this court cannot come to a conclusion that the accused No.1 to 4 has caused loss or damage to the property of BDA thereby the prosecution failed to prove the ingredients of offence under section 427 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.decision:
For the foregoing discussion an the findings to the above point No.1 to 3, this court proceeds to pass the following:
G K Vishwanath vs K N Prakash on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54414218/
9 ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
KABC030097562015 CC No.3659/2015 (i) The accused No.1, 2 and 4 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Section 447, 427, 420 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 33(A) of Bangalore Development Authority Act.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(v) Ordered accordingly.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
